# World reference

Every class in `assets/scripts/world/`, from its doc comments. The overview is in [README.md](README.md).

- [BodyNavFeeder](#bodynavfeeder)
- [KillFloor](#killfloor)
- [TerrainNavFeeder](#terrainnavfeeder)
- [WorldCoordinator](#worldcoordinator)

## BodyNavFeeder

`res://assets/scripts/world/BodyNavFeeder.gd`, extends [`Node`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node.html)

Puts a static body (a wall, a rock, a building) into the nav mesh.

Add it as a child of a StaticBody3D, the way [`TerrainNavFeeder`](#terrainnavfeeder) puts the terrain in. Its box shapes go into nav when it enters the tree and come out when it leaves; other shapes are skipped with a warning. Pawns then plan paths around the body, and a pawn walking the nav mesh (CrowdMover's C++ batch, NavWalking) slides along it instead of being handed to physics. Without it, paths go straight through the body and only physics stops the pawn. After moving the body by code, call `refresh()`.

### Functions

- `refresh() -> void`: Sends the body's boxes to nav again, from where the body is now. The nav tiles under it rebuild over the next few ticks.
- `box_faces(shape_transform: Transform3D, size: Vector3) -> PackedVector3Array` *(static)*: The 12 triangles of a box of this size, placed by the shape's transform. Each side is wound to face out (clockwise seen from outside, as Godot draws front faces), so nav takes the top as ground and the sides as walls.

## KillFloor

`res://assets/scripts/world/KillFloor.gd`, extends [`Node3D`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node3d.html)

A height below which pawns die, like Unreal's "kill Z".

Place one in a level at the height you want (its own Y), well below the lowest ground. A pawn that falls below it gets `kill_effect`, by default all its Health, so it dies the usual way (its Death ability, a respawn at a SpawnManager spawn point, a spawner's replacement). It runs on the authority only (the server, or offline), every `check_every_ticks` ticks, after every pawn has simulated; clients see the death in snapshots. With `report_falls` on, a warning says how the pawn got there.

### Settings and properties

- `kill_effect: Effect` = `<Object>`: What a pawn falling below gets. By default resources/effects/kill_self.tres, which takes all its Health. Another effect can do something gentler, as long as it moves the pawn back up or kills it: otherwise it gets it again on every check.
- `check_every_ticks: int` = `10`: How often it checks, in ticks written for 60 a second (converted to the match's rate). A pawn falling for a few ticks more before it dies makes no difference, and checking less often costs less with many pawns.
- `report_falls: bool` = `true`: On: each pawn caught here is reported in the Debugger, saying how it got here (see the class description). Off: nothing is reported, for a game where falling off the map is normal.

### Signals

- `pawn_fell(pawn: Pawn, report: String)`: A pawn fell below this floor and died here, with the report of how it got here (the same words as the warning). Sent only while `report_falls` is on. The replay recorder records it (ReplayGameplayChannel).

### Constants

- `GROUP = &"kill_floors"`: Every kill floor joins this group, so a replay recording can find them and record their reports.

### Functions

- `kill(pawn: Pawn) -> bool`: Gives a pawn the kill effect. Public, so a test or a game rule can use the same way of dying. True if it got the effect, false if it couldn't (no effect set, or a pawn with no Health or EffectManager).
- `fall_report(pawn: Pawn, last_seen: Variant, tick: int) -> String`: The words of a fall's report. `last_seen` is `[position, velocity, tick]` from the last check that found the pawn standing, or null if none did. Public, so a test can read it.

## TerrainNavFeeder

`res://assets/scripts/world/TerrainNavFeeder.gd`, extends [`Node`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node.html)

Feeds nav from a terrain generator, so that neither has to know the other exists.

[`TerrainGenerator`](../terrain/REFERENCE.md#terraingenerator) says when a chunk is built or removed; this hands its triangles to NavServer and announces its markers to NavMarkerManager. It also keeps nav built around every streaming source (within each one's `nav_distance`), and can tick NavServer (`tick_nav`). Normally a child of a [`WorldCoordinator`](#worldcoordinator), or of a TerrainGenerator with no coordinator. Give it a NavHooks to feed nav; with none it only announces markers, which need no C++ library.

With the tick driver running, nav goes with the ticks (state store spec 13.12): NavServer ticks once after each tick and the sources' interests are checked on ticks, so tiles land on the same ticks on every run; each tile landing goes in the [`LandingLog`](../state_store/REFERENCE.md#landinglog). Design: world spec (docs/world/WORLD_SPEC.md).

### Settings and properties

- `terrain: TerrainGenerator`: The terrain to feed from. If it's empty and this node's parent is a terrain, it uses the parent.
- `nav_hooks: Resource`
- `tick_nav: bool` = `false`
- `refresh_seconds: float` = `0.2`: How often to check where the sources are, in seconds.
- `unload_margin: float` = `64.0`: How far past a source's nav distance its nav stays built, in metres, so hovering around the edge doesn't rebuild it.

### Functions

- `uses_nav() -> bool`: True if this is feeding nav right now.
- `refresh_now() -> void`: Checks the sources now, instead of waiting for the next refresh.

## WorldCoordinator

`res://assets/scripts/world/WorldCoordinator.gd`, extends [`Node3D`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node3d.html)

Puts a level together from its parts: terrain, streaming and the nav feeder.

Add one to a level with these as children; it finds them by itself and wires them together, and builds nothing itself. Code reaches them as `world.terrain_generator`, `world.chunk_streamer` and `world.nav_feeder`.
- [`TerrainGenerator`](../terrain/REFERENCE.md#terraingenerator): required. It generates the ground.
- [`ChunkStreamer`](../streaming/REFERENCE.md#chunkstreamer): optional. It loads chunks around streaming sources; without it the terrain builds its fixed block.
- [`TerrainNavFeeder`](#terrainnavfeeder): optional. It feeds nav; without it there's no nav.

Tier 0 works with one terrain generator; interchangeable, eventually blended level generators are the end goal, not built. Design: world spec (docs/world/WORLD_SPEC.md).

### Settings and properties

- `terrain_generator: TerrainGenerator`: The parts. Left empty, each is found among this node's children.
- `chunk_streamer: ChunkStreamer`
- `nav_feeder: TerrainNavFeeder`
